title: Viral Isolation for SAR11 and OM43 Hosts
author: Holger Buchholz

To make up the PBS solution: Dissolve one tablet of PBS in 200 ml deionized water to create a solution with 0.01 M phosphate, 0.0027 M potassium chloride and 0.137 M sodium chloride, pH 7.4 at 25 C. Phosphate buffered saline Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #P4417-50TAB

To make a SYBR green working stock: Add 198 µl of sterile PBS solution (Step 23.1) and 2 µl of SYBR green in a 200 µl PCR tube to make up a working SYBR green stock. Make sure to wear gloves when handling SYBR green! SYBR® Green I nucleic acid gel stain Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #S9430 SYBR green is carcinogenic, handle with care!

steps.title: Initial Water Sample Filtration
steps.instruction: Filter 2 liters of environmental water through a 14.2 cm Whatman GF/D filter membrane using a peristaltic pump (e.g., Watson-Marlow Bredel 323Du) to remove large plankton and particles. Collect the filtrate in a sterile, acid-washed 2 liter polycarbonate bottle.

steps.title: Secondary Filtration
steps.instruction: Filter the collected filtrate through a 142mm Merck Millipore 0.2 µm PC membrane to remove larger bacterioplankton. Collect the filtrate in a clean, acid-washed 2 liter polycarbonate bottle.

steps.title: Viral Concentration
steps.instruction: Concentrate the 2 liter filtrate down to 50 ml using a tangential flow filtration unit (e.g., Sartorius 50R Vivaflow VF05H4) following the manufacturer's protocol.

steps.title: Final Viral Fraction Purification
steps.instruction: Filter the 50 ml concentrated sample through a 0.1 µm PVDF membrane syringe-filter to ensure a cellular-free viral fraction. Store water samples at 4°C in the dark for up to 8 weeks if not used immediately.

steps.title: Prepare Initial 96-Well Plate
steps.instruction: In a Cat II flow hood, prepare a sterile, acid-washed 96-well 2 ml Teflon plate.

substeps.instruction: Pipette 1 ml of sterile ASM1 medium into each well.
Add 100 µl (or 10% v/v) of the concentrated water sample as viral inoculum to each well in columns 1 to 8 (Viral Enrichment culture sets).
Leave wells in columns 9-11 without inoculum as no-virus controls.

steps.title: Inoculate Bacterial Hosts
steps.instruction: Inoculate the plate with exponentially growing bacterial cultures to a cell density of 1*10^6 cells/ml (T0).

substeps.instruction: Inoculate columns 1 to 11.
Leave column 12 blank as a medium control to check for contamination.

steps.title: Incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate at 18°C in an incubator without rotation for 2 weeks (approx. 336 hours) until no-virus controls reach stationary phase.

steps.title: Analyze for Infection via Flow Cytometry
steps.instruction: Determine if viral infection has occurred using a flow cytometer (e.g., BD Accuri C6 Plus).

substeps.instruction: Wipe the outside of the 96-well Teflon plate with 70% Ethanol and place in a Cat II flow hood.
Pipette 20 µl from each well of the Teflon plate into a corresponding well of a microplate.
Add 2 µl of SYBR green working stock solution to each well.
Incubate the microplate in the dark for 45 minutes.

Run the microplate on the C6 flow cytometer (approx. 2 hours) using these settings: Primary threshold FL1-H at 1000, no secondary threshold, ungated sample, medium flow rate 42 µl collection limit or 1 minute collection limit.
Compare no-virus controls to samples; look for increased noise, decreased host cell abundance, increased green fluorescence signal, or smearing/double peaks.

steps.title: First Round Enrichment
steps.instruction: If one or more wells in a Viral Enrichment set (columns 1-8) show signs of infection, isolate the virus for further enrichment.

substeps.instruction: Pipette all liquid from wells in columns 1 to 8 of the infected set into a 15 ml falcon tube.
Filter the liquid through a 0.1 µm PVDF membrane syringe-filter into another sterile 15 ml falcon tube to create a new viral inoculum.

steps.title: Second Round Enrichment
steps.instruction: Repeat the plating and incubation process using the new inoculum.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a new 96-well plate with 1 ml ASM1 medium per well.
Add 100 µl (or 10% v/v) of the new viral inoculum to columns 1 to 8; leave columns 9-11 as no-virus controls.
Inoculate columns 1-11 with bacterial hosts (1*10^6 cells/ml) and leave column 12 as a medium control.
Incubate at 18°C without rotation for 2 weeks.
Analyze via flow cytometry as described in the previous analysis step.

steps.title: Isolate Individual Viral Cultures
steps.instruction: For each well showing signs of infection in the second round, isolate the viral culture.

substeps.instruction: In a Cat II flow hood, pipette the contents of each infected well into individual sterile 1.5 ml Eppendorf tubes.
Filter each culture through a 0.1 µm PVDF membrane syringe-filter into a new sterile 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube, changing filter membranes and syringes for every sample.

steps.title: Serial Dilution for Purification
steps.instruction: Perform serial dilutions to isolate a single viral culture per row in a new 96-well plate.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 96-well plate as described in the plate preparation steps.
Add 100 µl (or 10% v/v) of a viral culture to column 1 of a row; mix gently by pipetting.
Transfer 100 µl from column 1 to column 2, mix, and repeat this process sequentially up to column 10.
Leave columns 11 and 12 without viruses.

steps.title: Final Purification Incubation and Analysis
steps.instruction: Incubate the dilution plate and identify the lowest concentration well showing infection.

substeps.instruction: Incubate the plate at 18°C without rotation for 2 weeks.
Analyze all wells via flow cytometry.
Identify the well in each row with the highest column number (lowest virus concentration) that still shows signs of infection.
Pipette the lysate from that specific well into a sterile 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube in a Cat II flow hood.
Filter the lysate through a 0.1 µm PVDF membrane syringe-filter into another sterile 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube, changing filters/syringes for every sample.

steps.title: Iterative Purification
steps.instruction: Repeat the serial dilution, incubation, and analysis process (Steps 14-20 in original text) two more times, using the lysate from the previous round as the new viral culture each time.
